title: Preity Zinta Recalls How Manisha Koirala Made Her Feel She 'Belonged' in Bollywood
excerpt: Ahead of her comeback film Vibe, Zinta told The Indian Express that Koirala's warmth on the Dil Se set gave her the confidence to start her film journey.
body:
• Preity Zinta told The Indian Express that co-star Manisha Koirala made her feel she "belonged" in Bollywood during the making of Dil Se (1998), recalling the warmth she received in her earliest days in the industry.
  • The actor is returning to Hindi cinema with Vibe, Kunal Khemu's action comedy releasing September 18, in which she plays an undercover agent named Madam H.
  • Vibe, produced by Amazon MGM Studios with Khemu's Drongo Films, also stars Kunal Khemu, Sparsh Shrivastava and debutante Vanshika Dhir; it is Khemu's second directorial after Madgaon Express.
  • Zinta, who moved to the US after marrying Gene Goodenough and was last seen on the big screen in 2018's Bhaiaji Superhit, is also awaiting Lahore 1947 with Sunny Deol.

Preity Zinta has opened up about the kindness that carried her through her first days in Bollywood — crediting Manisha Koirala, her co-star in Dil Se, with making her feel she belonged in an industry that can be unforgiving to newcomers.

In an interview with The Indian Express ahead of the release of her comeback film Vibe, Zinta recalled the support she received during her initial days, singling out Koirala's generosity on the 1998 Mani Ratnam set.

The comeback film

Vibe marks Zinta's full-throated return to Hindi cinema. Written, directed, produced and headlined by Kunal Khemu — his second directorial after the 2024 comic caper Madgaon Express — the high-stakes action comedy follows two hapless best friends who are unwittingly roped in by a mysterious undercover agent, played by Zinta, to protect India from a major terrorist threat.

Khemu, who revealed at the trailer launch that he had always been a Preity Zinta fan, said casting her was a leap of faith that paid off. "When I finished writing this film, and then it came to casting this, I had never seen her acting before. No one would have expected this. So, it'll be the best casting," he said, adding that she "looks lovely as Madam H." The film, produced by Khemu's Drongo Films in association with Amazon MGM Studios, also stars Sparsh Shrivastava and debutante Vanshika Dhir, and releases in theatres on September 18.

The Dil Se memory

Dil Se, Ratnam's romantic thriller set against the Assam insurgency, starred Shah Rukh Khan and Manisha Koirala, with Zinta making her debut as the bubbly Preeti Nair — a performance that won her the Filmfare Award for Best Female Debut. It was on that set that Koirala, already an established star, took the newcomer under her wing.

Zinta has spoken of that debt before. Congratulating Koirala on her performance in Heeramandi, she wrote on Instagram: "I love you Manisha... You are such a powerhouse of talent & an even better human being."

"I will never forget how lovely, welcoming & generous you were to me in Dil Se. Thanks to you I started my film journey on such a positive note."

— Preity Zinta, on Manisha Koirala

"You never made me feel I was working with a superstar & nurtured me on the shoot," Zinta added at the time — a sentiment she has now echoed again on the eve of her own comeback.

The winding road to stardom

As Zinta once clarified in an interview with Lehren TV, Dil Se was not technically her first signing. She had first been cast in Shekhar Kapur's Tara Rum Pum Pum, which was shelved, and had completed shooting Kya Kehna before Dil Se released earlier — "Dil Se was my third or fourth film, but it released earlier. So that's how it came."

What followed was one of the defining runs of the early 2000s — Soldier, Kya Kehna, Mission Kashmir, Dil Chahta Hai, Kal Ho Naa Ho, Veer-Zaara, Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna. Then, after marrying businessman Gene Goodenough and moving to the United States, where she is now raising twin children, Zinta stepped away from the screen, last appearing in 2018's Bhaiaji Superhit.

Why the story resonates

Mentorship stories are rare currency in an industry built on rivalries, and Zinta's tribute cuts against the grain of how Bollywood debuts are usually remembered. For the diaspora, the story has an added pull: Zinta is herself an NRI now, living in the US, and her return — in a film produced with Amazon MGM Studios for a global audience — mirrors the journey of many diaspora viewers who left India and are rediscovering its cinema. Vibe arrives in theatres on September 18.
